title: Europe Is Asking the Wrong Question About Russia’s Hybrid War
gist: Irdi argues the European debate over whether to call Russian drone and sabotage attacks 'hybrid war', 'acts of war' or terrorism misses the point: the binding constraint is a political threshold Russia keeps raising. He calls for a common European deterrence doctrine using energy sanctions, frozen Russian assets and military aid to Ukraine to raise the cost of each attack.

insights.claim: Russian pressure on Europe has shifted toward kinetic means (drones, explosives, infrastructure sabotage) and Moscow is now visibly less concerned with plausible deniability, historically a defining feature of hybrid operations.
insights.speaker: Beniamino Irdi
insights.so_what: Europe's security and defense-exposed assets face a higher, more openly attributed attack tempo; expect continued defense and counter-drone demand.
insights.locator: Over the past months, Russia's pressure on Europe

insights.claim: Germany attributed to Russia a failed August attempt to strike a Ukraine-bound cargo plane at Leipzig/Halle Airport with explosive-laden drones, and a Russian drone hit a train at Yahodyn on the Ukrainian side of the Polish border minutes after a train carrying former European leaders had left.
insights.speaker: Beniamino Irdi
insights.so_what: Concrete incidents show attacks now touching European logistics and rail corridors serving Ukraine; watch transport and airport security risk.

insights.claim: Moscow wants to be named as the perpetrator because it bets Europe's response will only highlight its own weakness.
insights.speaker: Beniamino Irdi
insights.so_what: Attribution without consequence strengthens Russian signaling; do not treat naming-and-shaming as deterrence.
insights.quote: Moscow does not care about being named.

insights.claim: Intelligence services warn of worse to come, including a limited Russian seizure of a small piece of Baltic territory backed by nuclear threats to test NATO's Article 5 credibility.
insights.speaker: Beniamino Irdi
insights.so_what: Tail risk for European risk premia, Baltic assets and defense stocks; the author reports it as a fear rather than his own forecast.
insights.locator: The result has been widespread alarm

themes.theme: The terminology debate is a distraction

insights.claim: Calls to retire the term 'hybrid' (Ischinger: these are acts of war; Estonia's Rosin: state-sponsored terrorism) do not address the real obstacle to an effective response, which is a political rather than technical threshold for retaliation.
insights.speaker: Beniamino Irdi
insights.so_what: Relabeling will not change policy; look for actual cost-imposing measures rather than rhetoric.
insights.quote: But the label is not what stands in the way of an effective response.

insights.claim: Hybrid campaigns work because no single attack crosses the threshold that triggers a serious response, and Russia has patiently raised that threshold over years; liberal democracies struggle to mobilize against a slowly rising tide.
insights.speaker: Beniamino Irdi
insights.so_what: Salami-slicing logic implies even an incursion on NATO territory could remain below the threshold if the trend continues.
insights.locator: Hybrid campaigns rest on a precise calculus

insights.claim: The real target of Russian kinetic hybrid attacks is the cohesion, political will and institutional credibility of the West, and a constant drone threat in public consciousness benefits the attacker regardless of any single strike's outcome.
insights.speaker: Beniamino Irdi
insights.so_what: Psychological and political effects, not physical damage, are the objective; gauge Western resolve through policy follow-through.
insights.locator: Renaming the problem does not change the dynamic

insights.claim: Europe needs a common deterrence doctrine for hybrid threats that makes each attack's cost tangible, predictable and higher than its benefit, using energy sanctions, seizure of frozen Russian assets, and less hesitant military aid to Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Beniamino Irdi
insights.so_what: Watch EU decisions on frozen-asset use and energy sanctions as the signals of whether deterrence is being built.
insights.locator: The task for Europe is to reverse the equation

insights.claim: The levers available to Europe are also vulnerabilities: the rule of law complicates action on Russian assets and voter-accountable governments hesitate over measures that raise energy prices, which Moscow exploits.
insights.speaker: Beniamino Irdi
insights.so_what: Expect slow, legally constrained action; energy-price sensitivity limits sanctions escalation.

insights.claim: A line Europe fails to draw below the Article 5 threshold is one the alliance, and the United States with it, may eventually have to defend above that threshold.
insights.speaker: Beniamino Irdi
insights.so_what: Under-response now raises the odds of a costlier, higher-escalation confrontation later.
insights.locator: This matters in Washington as much as in Berlin
